titles: He Traveled 5× Farther Than Marco Polo. Nobody Taught You His Name.
117,000 km Before Columbus: The Greatest Journey of the Middle Ages
The Man From Tangier Who Saw the Whole Medieval World
hook: You were taught that Marco Polo was the great traveller of the Middle Ages. Ibn Battuta, a young scholar from Tangier in Morocco, went almost five times farther: about 117,000 km by the usual estimate, across at least forty of today's countries. How did he pay for it, what nearly killed him, and why did Europe forget him? Told with animated maps, modern borders, a live distance counter, and the sources on screen. Distances and some stops (parts of China, the Volga trip) are estimates or doubted by historians, and we say so on screen.
